unmapped_findings: For the 17Al (Fe-35Mn-17Al-5Cu) alloy the peak Vickers hardness of the whole series was 924.9 ± 25.8 HV, achieved at 575 °C for 6 h (Table 3), which is a different aging condition from this 650 °C/10 h sample.

The indentation fracture toughness KIC of the hardest 17Al sample (575 °C/6 h, HV = 924.9) was 6.6 MPa·m1/2, calculated using Eq. (1) with E = 175 GPa for 17Al and an average crack length of 22 μm; this value is reported for the peak-hardness (575 °C/6 h) condition, not for the 650 °C/10 h sample.

The β-Mn in the hardest 17Al sample (575 °C/6 h) contained 16.3 at.% Al, 36.2 at.% Mn and 2.6 at.% Cu, with an average intrinsic (nanoindentation) hardness of 12.2 ± 0.1 GPa and an overall nanoindentation hardness H_Ave = 11.1 ± 0.6 GPa; these values pertain to the 575 °C/6 h condition rather than the 650 °C/10 h sample.
